ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY

Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.

ElementDescription: Do you start drinking to get over being depressed?
Are you able to control the amount you drink?
Notes: 0=Usually (or do not drink); 1= Often; 2=Sometimes; 3=Rarely or Never

ElementDescription: Do you lose control over what you do when you are drinking?
After drinking one or two drinks, can you usually stop?
How successful are you in stopping or diverting ideas, thoughts, impulses or images related to drinking when you're not drinking?
Notes: 0=Completely successful; 1=Usually able to stop with some effort; 2= I am sometimes able; 3=I am rarely successful with difficulty; 4= I am rarely able to stop even momentarily

ElementDescription: How much of an effort do you make to resist consumption of alcoholic beverages?  (Only rate your effort to resist, not your success or failure in actually controlling the drinking).
Notes: 0=I do not need to resist; 1= I make an effort to always resist; 2= I try to resist most of the time; 3= I give in without attempting to control, with reluctance; 4= I completely and willingly give in to drinking

ElementDescription: How strong is the drive to consume alcohol?
Notes: 0=No drive; 1=Some pressure to drink; 2=Strong pressure to drink; 3=Very strong drive to drink; 4=The drive to drink is completely involuntary and overpowering

ElementDescription: How much control do you have over drinking?
Notes: 0= I have complete control; 1= I am usually able to exercise voluntary control; 2= I can control it with difficulty; 3=I must drink and can only delay with difficulty; 4=I am rarely able to delay drinking even momentarily
